# DeepSeek Harness
English | 中文
## Community extension: session collaboration
This community fork adds session switching and parallel session collaboration to DeepSeek Harness. *
*Use the `codex/auto-session-switch` branch.** The `master` branch contains upstream code. This exte
nsion is maintained independently of DeepSeek AI.

- Start a fresh conversation or hand off with an Agent-authored summary and startup instruction.
- N

ame new worker, receiver, and successor sessions with an optional fixed title.
- Rename the current

session while keeping its history and continuing its work.
- Dispatch independent sessions in parall

el and send their results to an explicit receiving session.
- Keep a batch open for additional tasks

, then seal it to collect all results together.
- Preserve task and delivery records, explicitly res
ume interrupted work, and view delivered answers in the desktop client.
### Demonstrations
Two user-recorded desktop runs show `section top` dispatching to `section 1`, `section 2`, and `sect
ion 3`, followed by shared review in `section acceptance`. The Chinese GIF uses seconds 0–67.8 of it
s recording; the English GIF uses 0–36.5. Both play at 2× speed with a four-second final hold. The f
ull sidebar width preserves session creation, naming, and selection; unrelated workspaces are covere
d. Each GIF comes from one continuous recording. Playback speed does not represent response latency.
### Try the desktop extension
You need Git, Node.js `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0`, and pnpm `11.7.0`. Follow the desktop development pr
erequisites for your platform. Clone the feature branch:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Configure your model credentials in the client before sending a task. Later `pnpm run start:desktop`
launches reuse the enabled bundle. Importing a workspace alone does not enable it. These packages a
re not published to npm; the upstream npm command below does not install this extension. See the bun
dle guide for configuration and compatibility requirements.
### Try three workers and one collector
Paste this into a new conversation:
> Let’s try a parallel collaboration test. Name this session section top, then open three new sessio
ns named section 1, section 2, and section 3. Have each suggest a relaxing weekend activity and expl
ain why in one sentence. Put all three tasks in the same batch and, once they’re all done, send thei
r results together to a new session named section acceptance. Have it summarize the suggestions and
pick its favorite. There’s no need to read or change any project files.
The sidebar should show all five session titles. Open `section acceptance` to see the three suggesti
ons and its recommendation in the delivery card. Suggestions vary between runs. Background dispatch
does not change your selected conversation.
### Scope and limitations
The caller decides when to switch and prepares any external project state or worktrees. The plugin d
oes not merge code or treat delivery as acceptance. Switching waits for subagents, queued input, and
background jobs to finish. Parallel root sessions can continue independently. See the service refer
ence for recovery and routing behavior.
To report an extension issue, include your branch/commit, client version, original prompt, expected
result, and the affected task IDs. Remove credentials and private project content from any logs you
share. The extension source uses the repository's MIT license.
## Upstream DeepSeek Harness
DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness developed by DeepSeek AI.
It is built on an **everything-is-a-plugin** architecture and powered by Cordis, whose design is des
cribed in _A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability_.
Documentation: https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/
## Developer preview
DeepSeek Harness is in _developer preview_ and iterating rapidly. **THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREA

Review the safety notice before running the project.
